highlights.title: Rogue OpenAI agent 'infiltrated' Australian government website in world first
highlights.summary: Australia criticised OpenAI for taking "too long" to tell them about the breach which happened in June.
body: A rogue OpenAI agent hacked an Australian government website in June and accessed private data in what experts say is the first known case of its kind in the world.

The agent "infiltrated" a statistics portal containing "non-sensitive" data from Australia's universal healthcare scheme Medicare, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said in New York on Wednesday, local time.
He had a "very frank discussion" with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman for taking "too long" to disclose the breach and said there would be "legal consequences".
OpenAI said it only learnt of the breach in August while reviewing "misaligned model activity" and emailed a general inbox of an Australian government agency on 10 September.

highlights.title: The promise and peril of using visual AI to study cities
highlights.summary: In their new book, “How AI Sees the City,” the leaders of MIT’s Senseable City Lab examine the technology’s implications for researching urban life.
body: Images for download on the MIT News office website are made available to non-commercial entities, press and the general public under a Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives license. You may not alter the images provided, other than to crop them to size. A credit line must be used when reproducing images; if one is not provided below, credit the images to "MIT."

A few months ago, researchers from the MIT Senseable City Lab published a study about pollution in New York City featuring some new methods. For instance: With machine learning, they identified the types of vehicles appearing in 331 traffic cameras in the city, and estimated the emissions coming from each automobile. Given enough cameras, these visual artificial intelligence techniques could monitor emissions with an unprecedented combination of precision and scale.

For that matter, visual AI today can address all kinds of questions for urban planners. Why exactly is traffic snarling? What are the most dangerous aspects of different intersections? Which parts of plazas or parks attract the most people?
Across cities, more images means more data, more insight — and more concerns about privacy and fairness.

highlights.title: 'We have our own strengths' – Gordon backs Tuchel’s DNA comments
highlights.summary: Anthony Gordon has backed Thomas Tuchel's view that England's players have an inbuilt inability to control matches with possession - and has urged the team to embrace the country's traditional strengths.
body: Tuchel was criticised for England's defensive retreat after Gordon's goal gave them the lead against Argentina in the World Cup semi-finals, an approach which ultimately allowed their rivals to turn the match around in the final stages.

Tuchel responded by hitting out at the 'DNA' of English players. "I think ball possession plays a crucial role; it's maybe not in our DNA like it is in Spanish DNA or in Argentinian-Brazilian DNA, to take the ball and control the game with the ball," he said.

Tuchel made those comments despite leaving some of England's most technical players - Cole Palmer, Phil Foden, Trent Alexander-Arnold - out of his World Cup squad, and not giving midfielder Kobbie Mainoo a minute of game time during the tournament.
However, speaking ahead of England's Nations League opener with world champions Spain, Gordon has backed his manager's view.

highlights.title: Gremlins 3 Gets an Official Teaser, But There's Some Bad News
highlights.summary: Gizmo returns to the big screen after decades in the third Gremlins movie, but very little is known about the project. Even though the premiere is still a long way out, Warner Bros. has shared the first teaser for Gremlins 3.
body: Gremlins 3 is the first entry in the series in over 35 years. The last Gremlins movie, Gremlins 2: The New Batch, was released in 1990, six years after Gremlins. While the sequel wasn't as successful as the original Gremlins, the franchise has made millions and amassed thousands of fans in the past four decades. Gremlins has got it all: it's a Christmas movie with horror and comedy elements; there are freaky, but cool-looking creatures that create chaos for the sake of it, and an adorable, fuzzy main character who you just automatically root for.

While animated series based on its lore have been created, what fans have always hoped for is to see the beloved animatronic Gremlins in a third movie. It finally became a reality when Warner Bros. announced Gremlins 3 last year. The announcement included a Nov. 19, 2027, release date. Nearly a year after its announcement, Warner Bros. has now shared a first look at Gremlins 3 with a short teaser, which includes the announcement of a big delay for the movie's release, which will now happen on Oct. 6, 2028.

highlights.title: ‘The Eternaut’ Star Ricardo Darín on Argentina’s Resilience: ‘We’re Like Peter Sellers in ‘The Party,’ the Bugler Who Never Dies’
highlights.summary: The premise of Argentina’s Ricardo Darin’s latest feature, “Therapy Done Right” (Lo dejamos acá”), world premiering at the San Sebastian Festival, is deceptively simple: A pragmatic psychoanalyst loses faith in conventional methods and starts pushing the boundaries with his patients.
body: Ricardo, you play the psychoanalyst who rejects an award at the onset, stating that Argentina has the largest number of psychoanalysts in the world and yet the percentage of Argentineans with some form of mental health issue has doubled. Is this a fact?

Yes, and I think it has something to do with the mix of cultures that shaped Argentina – Italians, Spaniards, Jews, Arabs, Germans… – really, a bit of everything. And I think that’s part of where it comes from. Argentina also embraced psychoanalysis a long time ago, and it’s worked for us. In many ways, it’s worked really well.

Everyone has mental health issues. A lot of people around the world do – they just don’t realize it. They think there’s something else causing it. I think it’s worth clarifying that, because otherwise it might give the impression that Argentinians are the only ones with mental health problems. That’s not the case.

But I also know there are more psychoanalysts in Argentina. There are a lot of psychoanalysts compared to other countries. Why is that? Nobody really knows. Because people have been drawn to studying it at university. Argentina has some very good universities for psychology and sociology.

highlights.title: You be the judge: should my partner dial down the heat when he cooks?
highlights.summary: Rhonda believes Ned ruins woks. He reckons he has famous chefs on his side. You decide whose argument is in flames. • Find out how to get a disagreement settled or become a juror. He whacks the heat right up, which stains our wok and makes it really hard to wash up.
body: My partner, Ned, does most of the cooking in our house and he’s really good at it. I help prep and I usually do the washing up, which is how this issue arose. We had an old wok that became so encrusted with burnt stir-fry it was difficult to clean. Eventually, I said we needed to buy a new wok. We bought an expensive stainless steel one, but we’ve only had it three weeks and it’s stained already.

Ned cooks with the heat turned up as high as possible. I know with a wok you turn the heat up high initially before you put in the meat or vegetables, but you’re supposed to turn it down before you add the sauces. Otherwise, they burn on to the wok and make it difficult to clean. Once you get stainless steel to a certain temperature, it maintains that heat, so you don’t need to keep the flame on maximum. The point of stainless steel is that it stays stainless. If you stain it, you’re overheating it.

Once, when Ned was cooking, I turned the heat down myself. He objected and there was a bit of argy-bargy in the kitchen. I was annoyed because I knew I would be the one scrubbing the wok later, and I had a sore shoulder.

highlights.title: Meta is making a standalone Muse AI gadget
highlights.summary: Meta is building a dedicated hardware device for its new Muse AI agent. The product, called Muse Charm, was briefly shown off by Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg at the end of tonight's Meta Connect presentation.
body: The Muse Charm doesn’t require a phone, and it’s supposed to ship this year.

The Muse Charm has a fingerprint sensor on the top right corner that you can press to activate and begin speaking to the agent. There appears to be a small camera on the device as well, plus what looks like at least three holes for microphones on the front. Zuckerberg said you don’t have to unlock a phone or open an app to use the Charm, but he didn’t share how it’s actually connecting to Meta’s servers.

Meta plans to ship the Charm “in time for the holidays in December,” but as of now Zuckerberg says the company has “only built a few of these so far.” The company still needs to finalize “the finishing material,” he said. Throughout the keynote, he teased the device and made references to a translucent exterior that would let you see the gadget’s internals. He referred to it as an “elevated hacker aesthetic.”

highlights.title: 70 Years Later, The Greatest Closing Line In Fantasy History Is Still The Wisest Book Quote Of The 1950s
highlights.summary: The fantasy genre is built on unforgettable final acts that leave the stage in a blaze of spectacle. George R.R. Martin famously closes A Game of Thrones by spectacularly reawakening magic with the birth of dragons, while Brandon Sanderson caps the Mistborn trilogy with a universe-altering…
body: Instead of rolling the credits at the coronation of King Aragorn or the collapse of Barad-dûr, Tolkien meticulously winds the narrative down to a deeply personal scale. The hobbits return to liberate the Shire from Saruman's industrialized rot, only for Frodo to realize his psychological wounds are too deep to heal. The true climax isn't a battle, but a farewell. Frodo departs for the Undying Lands from the Grey Havens, leaving Sam behind to inherit Bag End. Sam simply walks back up the hill, opens his green door to his wife Rosie and daughter Elanor, and sits down. Tolkien closes the book with the simple phrase: “'Well, I'm back,' he said.”

highlights.title: Taking a deep dive in Helsinki’s subterranean city
highlights.summary: Under the Finnish capital lies a world of swimming pools, go-karting tracks, playgrounds – and even an art gallery. The moon is an impostor. Swimming backstroke beneath its surface, I look up at craggy hollows in close relief.
body: This is no lunar landscape but Helsinki’s underground swimming hall, excavated from granite bedrock and officially opened in 1993. These days, Itäkeskus uimahalli is one of the Finnish capital’s most visited leisure facilities, welcoming 400,000 people a year. Local people mingle with tourists, I will discover, during a week exploring Helsinki’s subterranean metropolis.

My visit was one of 12 research trips I made over three years to better understand how cities are being reimagined. It turned into a book, How to Build a City, for which I travelled to locations that are testing the frontiers of urban living in response to an increasingly uncertain world.

Many global cities feature a version below ground, but Helsinki’s is thought to be the only one transformed for peace. As urbanisation increased the population, a more efficient solution was needed for heating plants and telecoms cables. You could scatter them around in expensive pockets of land, digging up the streets and sacrificing parks. Or you could tuck them away beneath ground level, by adding to bomb shelters first carved out during the second world war.

highlights.title: Meta VR Glasses, Ray-Ban Meta Audio, Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3: Specs, Features, Prices
highlights.summary: At its Meta Connect event, CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced a handful of new smart glasses, including a slimmed-down VR headset and the company’s first camera-free glasses.
body: After months of controversy about the privacy of its smart glasses, Meta has unveiled the next iteration of its product lineup. At its Meta Connect event in Menlo Park, CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced all the new glasses the company is putting out into the world.

Its popular Meta Ray-Ban glasses are now in their third generation, but two new models steal the show: a powerful, slimmed-down version of Meta's Quest headsets capable of virtual and augmented reality modes, and a camera-free pair of Ray-Ban–branded smart glasses, called Ray-Ban Meta Audio. Meta is also bringing its Muse AI agent to its smart glasses platform.

The next evolution of Meta’s Quest VR headset is something truly different. Instead of a heavy helmet-like headset, the new Meta VR Glasses look like big goggles. They’re five times lighter than the Meta Quest 3. They sit on the nose, right in front of your face like glasses, with no headstrap needed.

They look and feel more like the virtual display glasses made by companies like Viture, and what Xreal’s Project Aura seems to be shaping up to be—lightweight mixed-reality lenses that let you access virtual spaces without the burden of a VR headset.

body: One very important thing to note about this set, though, is that the LEGO Smart Brick is not included with it. The set is compatible with it, though. Recommended for ages 9 and up, it comes with 885 pieces to create the starship with details like two stud shooters and foldout sections on top that allow you to get a good look at the interior.

Of course, the Millennium Falcon needs a crew, and this set comes with four minifigures to complete it: SMART Han Solo, SMART Chewbacca, SMART Luke Skywalker and SMART C-3PO. As you can tell by the 'SMART' at the front of their names, they can all be paired with the Smart Brick to hear extra sounds as you play. And as for hearing the ship, the set also comes with four SMART Tags.

highlights.title: Rachel Roddy’s recipe for tomatoes stuffed with breadcrumbs, chickpeas and herbs | A kitchen in Rome
highlights.summary: A well-seasoned and comforting meal to ease you into the autumn months. At this time of year, baked tomatoes stuffed with rice and surrounded by a packing-chip sea of potatoes are typical all over central and southern Italy, and in many other places besides.
body: I haven’t included sausagemeat in my version, but if you wish to, squeeze the meat from a couple of pork sausages and crumble it in at the same time as the chickpeas. Seasoning is fundamental here – salt, obviously (a small amount at various stages is better than all at once), as well as a little minced garlic and herbs. While my instinct here is for parsley and either rosemary or sage, dried mint also works wonderfully, as does cinnamon, whose warm, woody sweetness works beautifully with tomatoes, as it does in tomato sauce, but that’s another column.

How long the tomatoes take to bake will depend very much on their ripeness; harder ones need 10-20 minutes more than those with softer shells, but keep an eye on them and leave them to rest for a while before serving. I also think tomatoes stuffed this way benefit from being baked close together in a ceramic oven dish, which is why I baked cubed potatoes separately; some salted yoghurt or mashed courgettes or aubergine are also good accompaniments. As in the best and busiest tavole calde, serve the wrinkled tomatoes just hotter than room temperature.

highlights.title: A US-China AI Hotline Won't Be Ready For a While
highlights.summary: As the US and China race to become the dominant power in the AI industry, the countries also appear to be figuring out ways to communicate on national security issues.
body: As US president Donald Trump and Chinese president Xi Jinping prepare to meet in Washington for a state dinner at the White House on Thursday, AI has become a top priority. Tech executives from OpenAI and Nvidia have confirmed their attendance at the dinner, as a number of key agenda items are on the table.

Chief among them is a US proposal to establish an AI notification system with China, akin to the Cold War hotline with Moscow, which would allow each country to alert the other about national security issues related to AI. Treasury secretary Scott Bessent first announced the notification system on Sunday with Chinese vice premier He Lifeng.

But for all the high-level progress, Trump administration officials tell Inner Loop they expect it to still take a number of weeks to finalize an agreement, even if they are optimistic that the hotline could be in place before the year’s end.

There are several parts that need to be formalized in more detail, including establishing benchmarks on what kind of incident rises to the level of a national security issue, which remains unclear, as well as explicit sign-on from China, which has been noncommittal.

highlights.title: From Pet Care to Laundry: Why Everything’s Getting a Fashion Facelift
highlights.summary: From Stanley tumblers to luxury laundry, entrepreneurs are turning functional products into cultural brands — using collaborations, fashion-forward design and limited-edition drops to make the everyday desirable.
body: Whether it’s water bottles, pet care, alternative milk or laundry, some of the least glamorous corners of consumer goods are acquiring the kind of cultural cachet once reserved for fashion.

“When was it normal for a laundry brand to partner with Nobu? Never,” says Seyi Oduwole, foresight analyst at The Future Laboratory, referring to stylist-turned-entrepreneur Melissa Holdbrook-Akposoe’s laundry brand, Le Luxe. “But now, with Melissa’s brand identity tied to luxury selfcare, wellbeing and the elevation of the everyday, that’s normal.”

“Consumers still want quality and performance, but they also want products that reflect who they are. Utility and self-expression are no longer separate ideas. People expect both,” says Kate Ridley, chief brand officer at Stanley 1913. “A water bottle, a coffee cup, or a tote can be as intentional a choice as a pair of shoes or a favorite handbag.”

As fashion becomes crowded, and as consumers look beyond clothes for more accessible ways to express taste, the opportunity is moving into less expected corners of the consumer market. The next status symbol might not be hanging in your wardrobe, but sitting in your fridge, your cupboard, or your gym bag.

highlights.title: “Aristocrats on Mars”—Simone Rizzo and Loris Messina Share Their Vision for the “Moschino of the Future”
highlights.summary: Simone Rizzo and Loris Messina follow in the footsteps of Rossella Jardini, Jeremy Scott, and Adrian Appiolaza and Franco Moschino himself at Moschino.
body: It’s a deceptively simple distinction. For a house whose visual vocabulary has become so recognizable that its own jokes can easily become clichés, the temptation is to turn the archive into a dressing-up box: pick a slogan, throw in a windmill, and call it Moschino. Rizzo and Messina are taking the opposite route. They have looked at the clothes, studied their construction, and, as they put it, “metabolized” what they found. The objective is not reproduction. “We don’t want to reproduce anything he did literally. The only thing we are carrying forward is his spirit and his way of thinking.”

That may be the most revealing thing they’re saying about their new appointment. Because if Franco’s humor has been endlessly imitated, his method has been considerably less so. Rizzo and Messina are interested in the machinery beneath the joke. “For us it is fundamental that irony is in the concept,” they explained. “If irony is in the product, it becomes ornament.”

highlights.title: AI Agents Teamed Up to Cheat at Blackjack. Their Collusion Is Getting Harder to Spot
highlights.summary: A clandestine card-counting operation suggests we may need new ways to spot agent-to-agent deception.
body: This week I bring news of a daring casino caper hatched by a pair of rogue AI agents—as well as the clever trick that revealed their antics.

After researchers instructed them to count cards during a game of blackjack, the agents—which were controlled by the same model—developed a spontaneous secret code to help them get ahead. Though the episode happened inside an Oxford University lab, rather than a real casino, it has troubling real-world implications: It suggests that agents deployed in industries like finance and ecommerce could figure out how to partner up and cheat in ways that are difficult to detect.

“When taken individually, these agents may seem entirely [benign],” says Christian Schroeder de Witt, a computer scientist at Oxford University who led the work and who has done pioneering research into agent collusion. “Once put together in a group, they can collude secretly.”

highlights.title: Magic: The Gathering's 10 Best Counterspells, Ranked
highlights.summary: Over 30 years of game design, counterspells have evolved from straightforward two-mana hard answers into format-policing safety valves, color-pie-shattering oddities, and zero-mana emergency brakes.
body: Few feelings in Magic: The Gathering rival untapping your blue mana, passing the turn with a full hand, and watching your opponent wonder how many counterspells you’re ready to fire off. Counterspells are more than a defining part of blue’s color identity: They are the ultimate psychological weapon, transforming every spell an opponent casts into a calculated risk.

Separating casual staples from the absolute ceiling of power requires measuring raw mana efficiency, card advantage, and format-warping dominance across Legacy, Vintage, Modern, and Commander. From game-ending tempo swings to free-pitch spells that keep entire competitive formats honest, these are the 10 best counterspells in Magic history, ranked.

Magic is fundamentally defined by the color pie, a rigid set of boundaries dictating what each slice of the spectrum can do. Red is the color of chaotic emotion and aggressive reach, while blue holds a near-monopoly on stack interaction. Tucked away in the game’s earliest sets are the most efficient color-pie breaks in existence, like Red Elemental Blast and Pyroblast. For a single red mana, both cards let you either counter a blue spell or destroy a blue permanent.
